subject: Rebate vs Buyout: structured retention offer for CloudCrafters
messages:
From: Ellis Johnson <ellis.j@cloudcrafters.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@cloudcrafters.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive retention — request for match/creative structure

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're under a renewals push and our CFO wants a concrete counter to a one-time buyout that our current vendor offered: $650k one-time credit (plus rolling 10% off list for 12 months) in exchange for immediate termination and migration. The account team asked whether Redwood can match or provide a functionally equivalent package that keeps the economics intact but also preserves usage predictability for us.

High-level ask: can Redwood provide a structured retention package that blends an upfront credit, multi-quarter price protection, and a limited pilot for your Quantized-XL model (they want to keep cost parity for embedding-heavy workloads). They flagged three must-haves: 1) Guaranteed effective price per 1M tokens for 12 months; 2) An onboarding credit to offset migration costs; 3) A short pilot that ensures inference latency is within 150ms p95 for their typical traffic.

I've attached the competitor's redlined offer (competitor_offer.pdf). Hoping to get a ballpark today — procurement is on a tight clock.

Best,
Ellis
Procurement Lead
CloudCrafters Inc.

---

Note: procurement@cloudcrafters.com included for contracts coordination.
From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Ellis Johnson <ellis.j@cloudcrafters.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive retention — request for match/creative structure

Ellis — thanks for the details and the doc. Quick read-through: the competitor's $650k one-time credit is a big headline number, but it couples termination + 12 months of token discount structured as a rebate. We can replicate the economics without a unilateral buyout by combining: (A) a $300k transition credit to cover migration+eng hours, (B) a 9-month guaranteed effective price (tiered token bands) that yields ~equivalent unit cost to their offer at CloudCrafters' current run rate, and (C) a 3-month pilot of Quantized-XL with a Service Level Target for p95 latency at 150ms with rollback to an earlier model variant if not met.

I'd like to propose those as a starting point. Two internal constraints to flag: we usually don't do unconditional single-check buyouts, and any long-term price protection needs a committed minimum or staging of credits to protect our unit economics.

If that sounds reasonable, I'll draft a structured sheet (rebate schedule) and pull finance into the thread.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Lead — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Competitive retention — request for match/creative structure

Aditya / Ben — I reviewed the competitor_offer.pdf and ran a quick model. If we want to match the net economics for CloudCrafters' current usage levels (~18M tokens/mo), the math looks like:

- Competitor net present offer: ~$650k upfront credit + incremental ~10% token discount for 12 months = ~ $1.15M OG value over 12 months (depends on usage growth).
- Our equivalent structure (proposed):
  - $300k transition credit (applied against first invoice)
  - 9-month effective price protection resulting in unit rates that equate to ~ $800k value over 12 months at current run rate
  - $75k performance & migration services credit (applied as SOW credit)
  - Upside: if they commit to a 12-month minimum ARR band (6.5M tokens/month committed), we can layer a true upfront buyout credit to reach parity.

Two practical asks before we finalize numbers:
1) Ellis — confirm expected token growth (% per month) and whether embeddings are billed differently for you today (you mentioned embedding-heavy workloads).
2) We need a short legal-approved fallback clause for the pilot: if Quantized-XL can't meet the latency SLO on their baseline traffic after 2 test windows, we offer a one-time migration credit instead of penalties.

I'll attach a draft rebate schedule (proposed_rebate_schedule.xlsx) and a one-page summary for sales ops to sign off.

-Monica
Director, Sales Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Ellis Johnson <ellis.j@cloudcrafters.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@cloudcrafters.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive retention — request for match/creative structure

Aditya / Monica — thanks, this structure is helpful and closer to what we can take to legal. Quick answers:
- Token growth: expect ~5% linear month-over-month for next 12 months as a modest usage uptick.
- Embeddings: currently billed at same token rates but account has heavy vector/embedding calls (roughly 60% of tokens are embeddings from similarity searches).
- Pilot: willing to do a 30-day pilot; we'd need an SLA target in writing and a clause that if SLOs are missed twice, a $50k migration credit triggers.

We prefer the credit to be applied as an invoice offset rather than a separate prepaid account. Also open to the commit-based sweetener you mentioned (12-month minimum ARR band).

Ellis

On Tue, Jun 15, 2027 at 08:47 Ellis Johnson <ellis.j@cloudcrafters.com> wrote:

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: approvals & final packaging for CloudCrafters counter

Team — looping in final approvals. I ran the numbers with finance and legal; here's an internal-only summary (do not forward):

- Final suggested package to propose to CloudCrafters:
  1) $300k one-time transition credit (invoice offset)
  2) $75k SOW/service credit for migration assistance
  3) 9-month price protection that yields equivalent unit cost to the competitor given 5% monthly growth (detailed in the attached spreadsheet)
  4) 30-day pilot of Quantized-XL with a written p95 latency SLO at 150ms; if SLO missed twice, a $50k migration credit triggers (cap).
  5) Optional: convert to a $500k parity buyout if CloudCrafters signs a 12-month commit at minimum 6.5M tokens/month.

Rationale: this gives the customer near-parity economics, preserves our billing model (credits offset invoices), and avoids unconstrained upfront buyouts. Approve moving to a clean terms sheet + one-pager for legal to redline.

Ben Carter
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
